children: OTTAWA--Canada's annual inflation rate held steady in August as a slowdown in gasoline prices countered a rise in travel costs and rents.
The country's consumer price index rose 3.0% from a year earlier, Statistics Canada said Monday.
The steady pace in August was in line with what economists were expecting after inflation heated up in July to the top end of the 1% to 3% range the Bank of Canada aims for.
On a month-over-month basis, prices fell 0.1%, in line with expectations. On a seasonally adjusted basis, the consumer price index rose 0.2% from the previous month.
The Bank of Canada's preferred trimmed mean and weighted median measures of underlying inflation averaged 1.95% on-year, unchanged from the month before.
